course.title: Generative AI
course.subtitle: Wiki · PPGI058 · UFAL · 2026.2
course.tagline: The class wiki for Generative Artificial Intelligence. Each group has its own section and fills it in after presenting.

sections.name: Large Language Model
sections.description: Building an LLM from scratch, following Sebastian Raschka's Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch): the theory of chapters 1 to 3 and a hands-on class in notebooks, from the tokenizer to a GPT-2 that follows instructions.

children.name: Theory
children.description: The concepts behind LLMs, following chapters 1 to 3 of the book: what an LLM is and the Transformer architecture, how text becomes numeric input, and how the attention mechanism works.

children.name: Overview
children.description: The course roadmap, the three stages of building an LLM, and the presentation slides.

children.name: Ch. 1 · Understanding LLMs
children.description: What an LLM is, its applications, pretraining and fine-tuning, the Transformer architecture (BERT vs. GPT), zero-shot and few-shot, and the plan for building an LLM from scratch.

children.name: Ch. 2 · Working with text data
children.description: From raw text to model input: tokenization, vocabulary, special tokens, Byte Pair Encoding, sliding window, token embeddings, and positional embeddings.

children.name: Ch. 3 · Attention mechanisms
children.description: The long-sequence problem, Query/Key/Value, attention scores, self-attention, context vector, causal mask, and multi-head attention, with a worked numeric example.

children.name: Practice
children.description: The September 30 class in notebooks: building GPT-2 in practice. Each notebook builds a piece used by the next, from the tokenizer to the assistant that follows instructions, and answers the group's questions by running code.

children.name: Class setup
children.description: Map of the notebooks, who presents each one, how to install the environment, and how to prepare the checkpoints before class.

children.name: 01 · Tokenization and embeddings
children.description: Character, word and BPE tokenization; the GPT-4 and GPT-4o tokenizers; BPE from scratch; input/target pairs with a sliding window; token and positional embeddings.

children.name: 02 · Attention
children.description: Q, K, V and the score; other score functions (additive, cosine); causal mask; multi-head attention, number of heads and the non-divisible case; heatmaps of GPT-2's 12 heads.

children.name: 03 · GPT and generation
children.description: The GPTModel assembled block by block, text generation without pretraining, and architecture ablations: no LayerNorm, no FFN, ReLU instead of GELU, 12 vs. 24 layers.

children.name: 04 · Pretraining
children.description: Loss function, training loop, temperature and top-k, ablations with training, loading the official GPT-2 weights, and alternatives to the Transformer.

children.name: 05 · Spam classifier
children.description: Classification fine-tuning: replacing the output head with 2 classes, freezing layers, and an SMS spam classifier with about 96% accuracy.

children.name: 06 · Assistant
children.description: Instruction fine-tuning: prompt format, instruction dataset, training a GPT-2 that follows instructions, and where to find or how to create data.

children.name: 07 · Parameters
children.description: Why these values? The four GPT-2 sizes, where each parameter comes from, scaling by 3, bias and gradient, small vs. medium generating text, and other model families.
